the Broadway extension. The owner moved the vehicle to higher ground and relocated it from the area. It was CGFD/CGPD/CGFD who reported the vehicle in this area at 2:03 p.m.
Officers reported at 6:23 p.m. that a woman became ill after taking overdose medication offered by a male subject on Ohio Street. Police spoke with a man on Ohio Street who reportedly offered a woman medication and told her to “shoot it in your hand, I know it’s clean.” When the woman fell sick, she informed the police. The male subject then fled from the area. Officers combed the area for the suspect but had no success, obtaining no clues regarding his hiding spot.
An incident of domestic violence was reported on Sandusky Avenue. The male called three hours later to “let us know he’s okay,” and advised he has no plans on returning to the woman who reported the abuse. 7:28 p.m.
A man requested the police to go to an East Mary Street house where he claimed he feared abuse. When the man was agitated and drunk, he made the inquiries. The man admitted he was at the woman’s apartment for three days and told her he wouldn’t return because he cannot endure being mistreated, but he also seemed remorseful and acknowledged he could be aggressive and/or violent in nature. The male caller was given a summons for charges by the police, acknowledged and agreed to appear later, learned he needed to stay off the scene an additional hour, but then insisted the police go sooner to issue the summons, which they did. The male caller later returned and said he’d changed his mind and no longer wanted police to go there because “I’m already in enough trouble” from a known suspended violator at the scene, and he’d already been issued the summons to be at the alleged victim’s home. 7:05 pm.
